> A small card like device meant to resemble instant film. Using a led matrix and a mostly clean front, it would interact with the world and actions done to it, such as moving it around or turning it sideways, by making different visuals, showing the measured data, or even different faces, as I plan on making it be able to sense a few different things like temperature, inertial measurements, and potentially an ir sensor if possible. It would be a compact and simple device that would seem like an eager companion. This project is meant to push how well I can make a device compact, efficient, and interactive, all without using a prebuilt devboard.

## Design

### 2026-10-11 – I started creating the schematic, basing my device on the Starbie, however I switched the screen for an LED matrix built out of 6030 SMD LEDs in a 6 wide and 5 tall format, although I wanted to create

**2.83h**

I started creating the schematic, basing my device on the Starbie, however I switched the screen for an LED matrix built out of 6030 SMD LEDs in a 6 wide and 5 tall format, although I wanted to create a completely different device, I did not have enough time, so I went with the starbie as an example. I also finished routing the LED matrix and connected the routes to the XIAO rp2040. Next I will have to finish the schematic, finish routing the sensors, complete the BOM, and finish the firmware to make it show data from the sensors, act as a weak flashlight, and show an animation if possible.

### 2026-10-11 – I spent around 2 hours trying to work out python and a grid based fluid simulation to make my project have a cool fluid simulation "screen saver". I didn't get much progress considering how I barely k

**2h**

I spent around 2 hours trying to work out python and a grid based fluid simulation to make my project have a cool fluid simulation "screen saver". I didn't get much progress considering how I barely know python, but it was a learning experience letting me use my knowledge from lists in other things like block coding and basic knowledge, I might be able to develop my python skills enough to  work out how grid/array/matrix "cells" can affect their neighbors. I did not use any AI other than the autofill suggestions for things I already knew, I didn't want to cheat my way through since I need to know these things before I tackle more complex ideas, however I did use reference code from 10 minute physics which was in html to help me out.
